office/kestrel-clock-spec.docx._note_numbering: The markers are the numbers Word shows, not a repeated '1.'. CommonMark takes a list's start from its FIRST marker and counts up on its own, so writing '1.' on every item was only correct while nothing ever split the list; the nested step is 2.1, so its own marker is 1 and the step after it is 3.
office/kestrel-clock-spec.docx._note_emphasis: The source bolds only the second half of the identifier (a plain run 'Dma' followed by a bold run 'ArbiterUnit'), which is how Word actually stores partial-word formatting. Faithful output is therefore 'Dma**ArbiterUnit**'. The tradeoff is deliberate and recorded in docs/quality-plan.md: the emphasis is real information the document carries, and markdown_to_text strips the markers before tokenizing, so the identifier is intact in the text layer the index and the KB consume. What is lost is a raw grep of document.md for the unsplit identifier.

legacy/kestrel-clock-spec.doc._note_links: hyperlink measured to survive the soffice doc round-trip verbatim (text+url character-identical; also true for odt/rtf, probed on .doc as the binary representative). Observed on LibreOffice 6.4.7.2 — if a future soffice normalizes URLs (trailing slash, percent-encoding), this probe names the behavior change; adjust deliberately, never silently.
legacy/kestrel-clock-spec.doc._note_fidelity: pass, not unmeasured: the LibreOffice pre-convert lands on .docx, and the gate follows the EFFECTIVE extension. So a binary .doc is graded structurally too — and the probe proves the round-trip through soffice preserves heading levels, list nesting and table geometry, not merely the words.

pdf/kestrel-clock-spec.pdf._note_fidelity: unmeasured, not best-effort: there is no second implementation that can read structure out of a PDF, so nothing was graded and the block says so. best-effort would imply a measurement was taken on a best-effort basis. Derived, not observed — the PDF lane needs DOC2MD_PDF_PYTHON, which the office CI job does not set; assemble_bundle with source_structure=None produces exactly this block by construction.

pdf/kestrel-dataflow.pdf._note: TRUTHFUL CURRENT BEHAVIOR, not the desired one. office/kestrel-adversarial.docx._note: The document written to BREAK a naive converter, and it has already earned its place: on first conversion it found a real list-nesting defect (a bullet sub-list under a numbered step, carrying a different w:numId, was promoted to top level) at token_recall 1.0 with structural_errors 0 — invisible to every gate that existed before structure_fidelity. Every probe below is a measured value from a passing run, not a wish.
office/kestrel-adversarial.docx._note_renumbering: It then earned it again. The fixture now carries the five ways a procedure was silently renumbered — a screenshot inside step 2, a paragraph between two steps, a callout text box anchored in a step, a list declared to start at 5 (w:start), and numbering carried by a paragraph STYLE through w:basedOn — plus a table row that begins at grid column 1 (w:gridBefore) and a heading style only w:basedOn identifies. Every one of them used to convert wrong at token_recall 1.0 with structure_fidelity pass; the style-carried list was invisible to BOTH sides at once, which is why the gate agreed.
